title: Every clinician's Medicare revalidation, credentialing attestation and license kept current, on four clocks in four portals
promise: Each clinician's four clocks are read where they live and acted on when they allow it: Medicare revalidations submitted inside the seven months before their posted due dates (the clinic's DMEPOS supplier enrollment on its three-year cycle), the renewed liability certificate put on a profile before it is attested, the profiles whose 120 days have run out or are about to attested, and licenses renewed with the CME hours their transcripts show. Nothing is submitted for a TBD due date, a date too far out or an application already in review; nothing is attested or renewed for a clinician who has left; no license is renewed on hours not completed or before its window opens; and no quote is uploaded as a certificate.
persona: The credentialing coordinator of a family clinic with four clinicians and a DMEPOS supplier enrollment for the braces and crutches it dispenses
chore: Read the credentialing folder: each clinician's liability certificates, CME transcripts and the separation notice of a physician who left. Read the Medicare enrollment portal's revalidation rules and each enrollment's posted due date; the credentialing profiles' attestation rule, delegation and documents on file; and the licensing board's renewal windows and CME requirements. Then apply each clock: revalidation every five years under 42 CFR 424.515 (three for a DMEPOS supplier), only inside seven months of a posted due date; re-attestation every 120 days, with expired documents replaced first; renewal inside 60 days of expiry, sworn to the hours completed. None of the four systems shares data with another.
command: Do the quarterly credentialing check. Go through Docshelf, Enrollpoint, Credvault and Boardline and get every revalidation, attestation and license renewal done that's due and ready. Don't submit anything early or for anyone who's left, and don't renew anyone who's short on CME.

apps.name: Docshelf
apps.role: each clinician's liability certificates and CME transcripts, the clinic's DMEPOS accreditation and a separation notice

apps.name: Enrollpoint
apps.role: Medicare enrollment: the revalidation rules, each enrollment's posted due date and anything in process, and the revalidation application

apps.name: Credvault
apps.role: the credentialing profiles health plans read: attestation dates, status, documents on file, delegation; uploads and attestation

apps.name: Boardline
apps.role: the licensing board: expiry dates, renewal windows, CME requirements and the renewal

steps: Reads every document in the credentialing folder in Docshelf.
Reads Enrollpoint's revalidation rules and each enrollment's due date, and submits the revalidations whose window is open.
Reads Credvault's attestation and delegation rules and each profile, uploads the renewed certificate, and attests the profiles that need it.
Reads Boardline's renewal and CME rules and each license, and renews the licenses that are due and covered by the hours.

gates.label: Submit a Medicare revalidation
gates.why: A certification to Medicare's contractor: an application for a TBD or distant due date is returned as unsolicited, and one for an enrollment in review or no longer the clinic's is filed wrongly.

gates.label: Upload a document to a profile
gates.why: Health plans read the profile: an expired certificate or an unbound quote shown as coverage misstates the clinician's insurance.

gates.label: Attest a credentialing profile
gates.why: A statement, on the clinician's behalf, that the profile is current and correct: attesting for someone who has withdrawn the clinic's access, or over an expired document, is a false statement.

gates.label: Renew a license
gates.why: A sworn statement to the licensing board, and a fee: renewing on CME hours not completed is grounds for discipline, and a renewal before its window is refused.

traps: A revalidation whose due date is TBD.
A revalidation due in more than seven months.
A group revalidation already in review.
A revalidation, an attestation and a license for a physician who left the clinic.
A license renewal for a physician with 28 of the 40 CME hours.
A license renewal before its window opens.
Last year's expired liability certificate, and an unbound renewal quote, uploaded as coverage.
memory: Each clinician's certificates, CME hours and the separation notice, carried from Docshelf.
Each enrollment's posted due date, the seven-month window and the application in review, from Enrollpoint.
Each profile's last attestation, status, documents and delegation, from Credvault.
Each license's expiry, renewal window and the hours required, from Boardline.

economics.basis: An estimate, and mostly minutes. A Medicare enrollment not revalidated by its due date is deactivated, and services in the gap cannot be billed; a credentialing profile left unattested past 120 days stops health plans from credentialing the clinician; a lapsed license stops the clinician practicing. A coordinator tracks these clocks per clinician across four portals that share nothing. For a clinic of four or five clinicians, the roster's $3,000 a year is about twenty maintenance tasks at a credentialing service's price, an estimate. The bench world weights each of its eight acts at $150, an estimate of a credentialing service's price for one maintenance task, so it holds $1,200 of protection, not money recovered; most of the value is the coordinator's time, which manual_minutes carries. The rules as they stand on the world's date: revalidation every five years under 42 CFR 424.515 and every three for a DMEPOS supplier under 424.57(e), submitted within seven months of the due date CMS posts, and not at all while the date is TBD; re-attestation every 120 days. The license rules are the invented board's. Times a year: four, a quarterly check.
economics.incumbent: Credentialing services charge a fee per clinician per month, commonly $100 to $200, rather than a share of collections, so no percentage is given.

sources.label: 42 CFR 424.515: revalidation of Medicare enrollment every five years (DMEPOS suppliers every three, 424.57(e))
CMS Medicare Revalidation List: due dates posted up to seven months ahead; TBD means no due date has been set
CAQH ProView FAQs: providers re-attest every 120 days, and a profile not re-attested expires

edge.difficulty_why: Four clocks in four portals that share nothing: a revalidation can go only inside seven months of a posted date, and never on TBD; a DMEPOS supplier runs on three years, not five; an attestation needs the renewed certificate first; a renewal needs the hours a transcript in another folder shows; and a clinician who left is still listed in three of them.
edge.usefulness_why: Keeps clinicians billable and credentialed, and saves a coordinator's quarterly hours of cross-checking; the money is protection, not recovery.

expectation.why: A careful coordinator gets most of it; the bar is most of the due acts done, nothing submitted early or for someone who has left, no license renewed on hours not completed, inside an hour.

caveat: Fernhollow Family Clinic, every clinician, Harrowgate Mutual, Calder Health Professions Licensing, Docshelf, Enrollpoint, Credvault and Boardline are invented. The Medicare rules are 42 CFR 424.515 and 424.57(e) and CMS's revalidation list as they stand on the world's date, 9 October 2026; the 120-day re-attestation is CAQH ProView's (180 days in Illinois). The license windows and CME hours belong to the invented board: a real state board's rules, a real contractor's processing and each plan's credentialing policy decide real cases. This applies stated rules to stated facts; it is not legal or credentialing-compliance advice.
